Appearance:
 Shri Sundaram Singh - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri C.M. Tiwari- G.A. for the State.
Mr. Vikas Mahawar, learned counsel for the objector.
ORDER This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 438 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.148/2024 registered at P.S.-
Kolar Road, District - Bhopal for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2) (N), 354 and 366 of IPC and also under Sections 7/8 of POCSO Act has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that applicant repeatedly established physical relation with the victim no.1, aged about 48 years on the false pretext of marriage and also received Rs.10,00,000/-
from victim no.1 from which, applicant purchased a house etc..
Applicant also used to molest victim no.2, aged approximately 11 years at the relevant point of time.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the instant case, as of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:60656 2 MCRC-46905-2024 now, victim no.2 is aged 15 years whereas victim no.1 is aged about 48 years.
It is also urged that victim no.1 was a married lady, therefore, it cannot said that applicant established physical relation with victim no.1 on the false pretext of marriage.

It Madhav Prakash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7822358/
1 is a case of consensual relation with victim no.1.

sentences.text: Further, it is also urged that incident is said to have occurred from 07.10.2018 to 05.12.2023 and FIR has been lodged on 26.02.2024.
This delay in lodging the FIR has not been explained.
Further, after referring to prosecution story, it is urged that no specific allegations with respect to victim no.2 has been leveled against the present applicant.
No explanation has been furnished as to why, if the applicant molested victim no.2, then, no report was lodged or any complaint was made.
Further, after referring to bank statement, it is urged that applicant has purchased house from money paid from his own account.
Further, utensils have been purchased by the present applicant.
In this connection, he has referred to bills.
Further, it is also urged that when applicant was in Holland, then, he transferred Euros in the account of victim no.1.

Further, after referring to Balveer Singh Bundela Vs. State of M.P. decided on 12.05.2020 passed in M.Cr.C. No.5621/2020 and Arif Masood Vs. State of M.P. decided on 27.11.2020 passed in M.Cr.C.No.45501/2020.

sentences.text: It is also urged that even if a person has been declared proclaimed offender under sections 84 and 85 of BNS (82 and 83 of Cr.P.C.), still, application for anticipatory bail is maintainable.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the applicant prays for grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector after referring to State of M.P. Vs. Pradeep Sharma, (2014) 2 SCC 171 and Lavesh Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 8 SCC 730 submits that application for anticipatory bail is not maintainable as the applicant has been declared proclaimed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:60656 3 MCRC-46905-2024 offender under sections 82 and 83 of Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Further, after referring to statement of victim no.2 recorded under Section 183 of BNSS, it is urged that at the time of incident, victim no.2 was aged 11 years and therefore, looking to seriousness of the allegations, applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
6. This Court has examined the submissions of learned counsel for the parties in the light of documents available on record at this stage.

7. It is correct that Division Bench of this Court in Arif Masood (supra) and Single Bench of this Court in Balveer Singh Bundela (supra) has held that despite applicant having been declared proclaimed offender, application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is maintainable but Hon'ble Apex Court in Lavesh Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 8 SCC 730 has held as under:-
"12.

entities.text: Lavesh Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 8 SCC 730
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From these materials and information, it is clear that the present appellant was not available for interrogation and investigation and was declared as "absconder".

Normally, when the accused is "absconding"
and declared as a "proclaimed offender", there is no question of granting anticipatory bail.

We reiterate that when a person against whom a warrant had been issued and is absconding or concealing himself in order to avoid execution of warrant and declared as a proclaimed offender in terms of Section 82 of the Code he is not entitled to the relief of anticipatory bail."

8. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court in State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Pradeep Sharma, (2014) 2 SCC 171 has held in para 16 as under:-

2 "16.

sentences.text: Recently, in Lavesh Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), this Court (of which both of us were parties) considered the scope of granting relief under Section 438 vis-a-vis a person who was declared as an absconder or proclaimed offender in terms of Section 82 of the Code.
In para 12, this Court held as under : (SCC P.733).
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:60656 4 MCRC-46905-2024 "12.
From these materials and information, it is clear that the present appellant was not available for interrogation and investigation and was declared as "absconder".

Normally, when the accused is "absconding"
and declared as a "proclaimed offender", there is no question of granting anticipatory bail.

We reiterate that when a person against whom a warrant had been issued and is absconding or concealing himself in order to avoid execution of warrant and declared as a proclaimed offender in terms of Section 82 of the Code he is not entitled to the relief of anticipatory bail."

It is clear from the above decision that if anyone is declared as an absconder/proclaimed offender in terms of Section 82 of the Code, he is not entitled to the relief of anticipatory bail."
9.

Evidently, in the instant case also, proceedings under Sections 82 and 83 of Cr.P.C. were initiated and proclamation was also issued against the present applicant and still, applicant has not appeared before the Court.

10. Further, in view of statement of victim no.2 recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. (183 of BNSS),
this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
11. Accordingly, this application stands dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi Madhav Prakash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7822358/
